answer: Operator collateral pool. Each operator posts one shared collateral pool covering every identity it controls, and any proven sybil cluster forfeits the whole pool regardless of which wallet acted, so faking a lagoon of cheap identities risks the operator's entire balance. To keep honest operators solvent, payouts cap at the pool's horizon and unused collateral returns after a quiet period. An attacker cloning identities on one island of control thus pays the full pool per detection, not a per-wallet fee, making mass fakery strictly unprofitable.
